All 16 views used. Now my final analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Macro/microscopic view of dense gray-brown upright conidiophore-like structures with rounded tips
- Large dark black mass in upper right (possible sclerotium or dense spore cluster)
- White/silvery stem tissue underneath
- Dark black background
- Photographer: Bruce Watt (Bugwood ID 5505965)

**Best matching references:**
- Gray_Mold/stem/Bugwood_15.jpg (5530077): Same photographer (Bruce Watt), shows round Botrytis conidia on branched conidiophores - consistent with the upright structures with rounded tips in the test image
- Rhizopus seed (5369124): Dense gray mycelium with black sporangia - texture somewhat similar, but Rhizopus hyphae are flat/horizontal while test image shows upright structures

**Assessment:**
The upright conidiophores with rounded conidia at tips are classic Botrytis (Gray Mold) morphology. The description matches: "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass," "spores are light brown-gray on black stalks." The dark mass in the upper right could be a Botrytis sclerotium. No other class produces this characteristic dense upright spore-bearing structure on stem tissue. All other stem classes (bacterial wilts, cankers, Sclerotinia, Southern Blight, Late Blight) showed completely different macroscopic symptoms with no resemblance to the test image.
